title: Resolve, one recorded run
sop: KYB onboarding SOP (sop/kyb_sop.md), the approved spec spec/kyb-v1.json and the six example case files

steps.title: Z3 checks the SOP
steps.result: Z3 finds 3 problems in version 1 of the rules.
steps.text: Resolve runs Z3, a logic solver, on the rules in use today (version 1) and works out a decision for each of six example case files. Z3 checks every case up to a size limit, not just the six examples.

steps.title: Claude writes the questions
steps.result: Claude writes a question and two options for each problem.
steps.text: For each problem, Claude writes a question for the policy owner in plain words, two options, and the rule change each option would make. Claude only proposes: Resolve rejects a change that doesn't load or doesn't quote the procedure.

steps.title: Resolve shows what each option would change
steps.result: All 6 options are checked before the owner answers. Letting a verified licence count fixes two problems at once, but would open a new one.
steps.text: Before the owner answers, Resolve applies each option's edit and runs Z3 again: does the problem go away, does the edit cause a new one, and which example cases would get a different decision.

steps.title: The owner answers, and Resolve writes version 2 of the rules
steps.result: Two answers clear all three problems and become version 2, a draft. One example case flips to approve, and Z3 finds one new gap.
steps.text: Resolve never edits the rules in use. It saves the answers as version 2, a draft, and version 1 stays in use until the owner approves a replacement. The licence answer settles two problems at once, because both came from the same conflict between 5.2 and 5.3. It also opens the gap step 3 warned of: what to do while a licence check hasn't come back.

steps.title: Claude asks about the new gap
steps.result: Claude asks the owner what to do while a licence check is still open.
steps.text: Version 2 approves a money services business whose licence is verified, but doesn't say what to do before the check comes back. Claude writes a question and two options for that.

steps.title: Resolve shows what each option would change
steps.result: Waiting for the licence check closes the gap. Escalating now leaves the rules as they are.
steps.text: As in step 3, both options are checked against version 2 before the owner answers.

steps.title: The owner answers, and Resolve writes version 3
steps.result: The owner chooses to finish the licence check first. That gives version 3, and Z3 finds no problems left.
steps.text: Each round of answers makes a new version, so this second round gives version 3. Like version 2, it isn't in use until the owner approves it.

steps.title: The owner approves version 3
steps.result: The owner approves version 3, and it replaces version 1 as the rules in use.
steps.text: The approval is tied to the exact text the owner reviewed, so if version 3 changed afterwards the approval wouldn't count. Cedar Ridge's case file still says escalate because it was decided under version 1, so Resolve flags it to be run again under the new rules.
